messages:
ops-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — High GPU queue growth in us-west-2 layer (autoscaler not recovering). Pager triggered: PAGERDUTY #12345.

maria (oncall): I'm seeing tail latency spike ~2.1s and queue length creeping from 400 -> 2.1k over last 6m. Any recent deploys?

ajay: No deploys in the last 30m. Autoscaler logs show repeated scale attempts that end with nodes becoming NotReady. suspect driver/kernel flaps.

infra-bot: autoscaler: attempted 5 scale-ups; 3 nodes joined then flapped (kubelet lost). Eviction rate high.

samir: getting CUDA/Xid 13 on several pods, then OOM killer on driver process. snippet from node-12 logs:
```
[  123.456789] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 13, PID 23456, GPU 0
E tensorflow: out of memory while allocating 1.2GiB
```

maria (oncall): ok — that explains effective capacity drop. If nodes join then add zero capacity, autoscaler keeps pushing and we hit max scale. We need immediate mitigation to stop cascade.

tess: Agreed. Temp mitigation plan: 1) Pause autoscaler scale-ups, 2) Cordon problematic nodes, 3) Apply driver revert/hotpatch to new nodes or route traffic away to other region. Thoughts?

ajay: +1. Pause: `kubectl scale deploy autoscaler --replicas=0 -n infra` (we can do a pause flag but quick scale to 0 blocks new nodes). Also set risk mode on ingress to 503 fallback when queue > 1500.

samir: I'm patching node pool config to pin to previous driver build (rnv-2026-03-01). New machines will come up with that image. Starting cordon/evict on affected nodes (node-10..node-14).

maria (oncall): Doing customer impact assessment now. Which customers hitting errors? ops-bot: CI -> top routes: /chat/completions (60%), /embed (30%). Errors translate to timeouts for mid-tier customers (3 customers > 5% error).

ops-bot: Customer impact summary: 3 customers experiencing elevated 5xx and timeouts. Temporary mitigation: rate limit to 60rps for non-enterprise keys. Notifying account managers.

tess: I'm standing up temporary capacity in eu-west-1 and will shift low-priority traffic. ajay can you update routing rules?

ajay: On it. Added region-fallback: low-priority buckets -> eu-west-1, high-priority pinned. Rolling change now (1/3 routes).

maria (oncall): Quick checklist for live ops (I'll run):
- pause autoscaler scale-ups ✅
- cordon/evict affected nodes ✅
- revert to driver image on new nodes (samir) — in progress
- temporarily reroute low-priority traffic ✅
- increase logging & capture heap traces for driver process (samir) — collecting
- page infra-svc to review autoscaler limits tomorrow (postmortem)

samir: Collected kernel oops + nv driver heap snapshot. Pushing hotpatch to staging nodes, will validate on 2 nodes then allow scale-ups.

maria (oncall): Customer-facing note draft: "We're investigating intermittent timeouts and increased latencies due to GPU driver instability affecting autoscaling. We've implemented routing and throttling to reduce impact and are rolling a driver hotpatch. We'll update in 30 mins." Anyone edit?

tess: Add estimated ETA: 90m for full mitigation and note that enterprise customers unaffected due to capacity reservations.

ops-bot: Update: Hotpatch validated on 2 nodes, no Xid observed for 12m. Ready to allow limited scale-ups.

maria (oncall): Re-enabling autoscaler in probe mode: `kubectl scale deploy autoscaler --replicas=1 -n infra`. Monitor queues closely — if Xid returns, we'll immediately scale back and re-cordon.

ajay: Autoscaler probe allowed. New nodes launching with pinned driver. Watching metrics.

(10m later)
ops-bot: Queue stabilized 2.1k -> 300 over 12m. 5xx rates down to baseline. No new Xid in patched nodes.

maria (oncall): Good work. Next steps: full rollback of pause, lift region fallback once stable, and run a root-cause postmortem. Assign: samir to driver investigation, ajay to autoscaler tuning, tess to comms.

samir: Filing bug and capturing repro harness. Likely a regression in nv-driver 540.2 -> 541.x under sustained batching. Will include kernel traces.

maria (oncall): Closing incident channel for now — we'll reopen if regressions appear. Postmortem ping scheduled in #postmortems. :thumbsup:
